headline: Biomes are Earth's life zones—each with distinct climate, plants, and animals
universal_truth: Environment shapes what can thrive; match your nature to your environment or change one of them
fun_facts: There are roughly 10-15 major biomes on Earth, from tundra to tropical rainforest
Rainforests cover only 6% of Earth's surface but contain over half of all species
The same latitude can have very different biomes depending on ocean currents and altitude
discussion_questions: What 'biome' do you thrive in—work environment, social setting?
Have you ever been in the wrong environment for your nature?
How do you adapt to different environments?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Polar bears don't live in deserts. Cacti don't grow in rainforests. Earth is divided into biomes—regions with distinct climates and life forms. Each biome selects for different traits. Environment determines what can thrive.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Species are matched to their biomes. Put them in the wrong one, and they struggle. What does this teach about environment and success?

options.text: Success depends heavily on environment fit—traits that succeed in one context may fail in another; matching your nature to your environment is strategic
options.response: Yes. A polar bear in a desert dies—not because it's a bad bear, but because it's in the wrong biome. Environment fit matters as much as individual ability.
Strength helps, but even the strongest are shaped by environment...

q1.title: Climate Shapes Life
q1.script: Temperature, rainfall, and seasons determine what can live where. Tropical rainforests are wet and warm—lush growth. Deserts are dry—specialized survivors. Climate sets the rules.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Climate Shapes Life"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Local Adaptation
q2.script: Each biome has species adapted to its specific conditions. Arctic foxes have thick fur. Desert plants store water. Adaptation to local conditions beats generic capability.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Finding Your Biome
q3.script: You have a biome too—environments where you thrive. Some people flourish in competitive environments; others in collaborative ones. Finding the right environment unlocks potential.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Environment shapes what can thrive. Match your nature to your environment—or change one of them. Fit matters.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 258. Tomorrow, we'll explore why variety matters—biodiversity. Until then, consider what environment brings out your best.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Environment Audit - Where Do You Thrive?
growTrack.activity: What environments bring out your best? Fast-paced or steady? Social or solo? Structured or flexible? Are you currently in a biome that matches your nature? If not, can you change environment or adapt yourself?
